desc: Analyze small cases (brute-force BFS mentally or on paper) for X=Y=1, X=1,Y=2, X=2,Y=2 to detect invariants beyond popcount.
Model as run-length sequence; define how operations change run lengths (split/merge) and derive a canonical form (e.g., move all possible 1s left).
Optimize `canonical` to O(N) by maintaining run-length encoding on the stack (merge runs after each rewrite) instead of raw characters.

Verify the run-stack normal-form algorithm against brute-force BFS for small N, X, Y (all binary strings, N ≤ 10, X,Y ≤ 3): reachability iff equal canonical form; specifically test cascading cases like 0^(2X) 1^Y and r==0 merge chains.

Clean up the solution code: remove stale exploratory comments, keep only the final O(N) run-stack canonicalization with a concise correctness comment, and re-verify edge cases (N < X+Y, X+Y == N, all-0/all-1, X=Y=1 reduces to popcount, runs much longer than X/Y).
